summary: Just as real as the flow of blood through human veins is our curiosity about the unknown; ever since the dawn of humanity, we have looked upward and asked questions, then gone on to do the impossible to satisfy that curiosity—creating machines to serve as our assistants, capable of reporting back from places beyond the reach of our own eyes. Keeping a young audience informed—via a dedicated portal—with compelling stories about actual space travel is a vital objective for fostering, in time, that thirst for discovery we feel when we look upward.
details:
What does it do, or how does it work? It presents—in a fascinating way, via a web portal—the stories of devices sent from Earth, which now serve as silent, distant witnesses to humanity’s desire for knowledge.

What benefits does it offer? It fosters interest in aerospace science and its history among young people, encouraging them to explore the subject further.

What is the project’s intended impact? To reach a broad audience of young people and engage them with topics related to the vehicles sent into space.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used to develop the project? Python was used, along with standard home computing equipment.

In what way is the project creative? It is creative in that it sparks the imagination, captivates the reader, and inspires a desire to learn more about space exploration.

What factors did your team take into account? The team considered the current need among young people to satisfy their curiosity with extraordinary subjects—specifically, the human-made devices currently operating on other planets.
